title: 7.1 Small Group · Group 1
contentObjective: With my small group, I can use integers to represent quantities in everyday life, explain what 0 means in each situation, and name the opposite of an integer on the number line — one step at a time, with support.
languageObjective: I can talk through each step out loud using a sentence frame and the lesson's key words.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — How do you use integers to describe quantities above and below zero?
conceptIntro.intro: Counting numbers, their opposites, and 0 are integers. A negative integer is less than zero and is written with a − sign. Opposites are the same distance from 0, but on opposite sides of the number line. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Pick what 0 means in the situation first. Then a quantity above 0 is a positive integer and a quantity below 0 is a negative integer, and its opposite is the same distance from 0 on the other side.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Badwater Basin is 86 meters below sea level, and sea level is defined as 0.
Below 0 means a negative number, so I write the elevation as −86 meters.
On a number line, I count 86 units to the LEFT of 0 and mark that point.
The opposite of −86 is 86. Both are 86 units from 0, just on different sides.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: One day in January the temperature in Toronto was 9°C and in Reykjavik it was −9°C.
Which one is to the left of 0 on the number line? The negative sign tells us: −9.
How many units from 0 is 9? How many units from 0 is −9? Both are 9 units.
So 9 and −9 are opposites — same distance from 0, opposite sides.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "The multiples/steps I need are ___ , and the answer is ___ ."

youDo.title: Now you try — with support
lines: Try the practice problems below. The hint button is right there whenever you get stuck — use it, that's smart.

Remember the key idea: Pick what 0 means in the situation first. Then a quantity above 0 is a positive integer and a quantity below 0 is a negative integer, and its opposite is the same distance from 0 on the other side..

explore.instructions: Quick warm-up together: Each card names a real quantity. Sort it by whether the integer that represents it is BELOW zero, ABOVE zero, or exactly AT zero.
explore.instructionsEs: Cada tarjeta nombra una cantidad real. Clasifícala según si el número entero que la representa está DEBAJO de cero, ARRIBA de cero o exactamente EN cero.

items.text: Badwater Basin: 86 meters below sea level
Reykjavik in January: 9 degrees below zero
A football play with a 10-yard loss
Toronto in January: 9 degrees above zero
A hiker 250 meters above sea level
A football play with a 21-yard gain
The water surface at sea level
A play that gains no yards at all

explore.label: Sort each real-world quantity by where its integer lands compared to 0.
explore.explanation: In every one of these situations, 0 is a chosen starting point: sea level, zero degrees, or the line of scrimmage. Quantities described as 'below', 'a loss', or 'under' land to the left of 0 and take a − sign, so they are negative integers. Quantities described as 'above' or 'a gain' land to the right of 0 and are positive integers. Two cards describe exactly the starting point itself, so their integer is 0 — which is neither positive nor negative.
explore.explanationEs: En cada una de estas situaciones, 0 es un punto de partida elegido: el nivel del mar, cero grados o la línea de golpeo. Las cantidades descritas como 'debajo', 'una pérdida' o 'bajo' quedan a la izquierda del 0 y llevan signo −, así que son enteros negativos. Las cantidades descritas como 'arriba' o 'una ganancia' quedan a la derecha del 0 y son enteros positivos. Dos tarjetas describen exactamente el punto de partida, así que su entero es 0, que no es ni positivo ni negativo.

diagram.intro: Drag the point to any integer. Watch its distance from 0 and its opposite — −9°C in Reykjavik and 9°C in Toronto sit the same distance from 0 on opposite sides.

approaching.stem: Badwater Basin is 86 meters below sea level, and sea level is 0. Which integer represents that elevation?
approaching.explanation: Below sea level means less than 0, so the elevation is written with a negative sign: -86 meters.
choiceFeedback: This is 86 meters ABOVE sea level. Dropping the negative sign moves the point to the wrong side of 0.
Zero is sea level itself, the surface of the water — not a spot 86 meters underneath it.
The digits got reversed here: the sign is right but the distance is not. The sign says 86 meters, not 68.
hints: Sea level is 0. Is 'below sea level' more than 0 or less than 0?
Numbers less than 0 are negative numbers and are written with a − sign in front.
Keep the distance the sign gives you — 86 meters — and add the symbol that shows the point is below 0.
approaching.stemEs: Badwater Basin está 86 metros bajo el nivel del mar, y el nivel del mar es 0. ¿Qué entero representa esa elevación?
approaching.explanationEs: Bajo el nivel del mar significa menos que 0, así que la elevación se escribe con signo negativo: -86 metros.
hintsEs: El nivel del mar es 0. ¿'Debajo del nivel del mar' es más de 0 o menos de 0?
Los números menores que 0 son números negativos y se escriben con un signo − delante.
Conserva la distancia que da el letrero — 86 metros — y agrega el símbolo que muestra que el punto está debajo del 0.

approaching.stem: In Reykjavik the temperature was -9°C. What is the opposite of -9?
approaching.explanation: The opposite of a number is the same distance from 0 on the other side, so the opposite of -9 is 9.
choiceFeedback: A number cannot be its own opposite unless it is 0. The opposite of a negative number is on the other side of 0, so it is positive.
Zero is its own opposite, but it is not the opposite of -9 — it is 9 units away from -9, not on the far side of 0.
Doubling the distance from 0 is not the same as crossing to the other side. The opposite keeps the distance 9 and only changes the direction.
hints: 'Opposite' means the same distance from 0, but on the other side of 0.
-9 sits 9 units to the LEFT of 0. Count 9 units to the RIGHT of 0 instead.
Keep the 9 exactly the same and change only the direction, which means changing only the sign.
approaching.stemEs: En Reikiavik la temperatura era -9°C. ¿Cuál es el opuesto de -9?
approaching.explanationEs: El opuesto de un número está a la misma distancia de 0 pero del otro lado, así que el opuesto de -9 es 9.
hintsEs: 'Opuesto' significa la misma distancia del 0, pero al otro lado del 0.
-9 está a 9 unidades a la IZQUIERDA del 0. Cuenta 9 unidades a la DERECHA del 0 en su lugar.
Conserva el 9 exactamente igual y cambia solo la dirección, lo que significa cambiar solo el signo.

choices: A number written -0, which is less than 0
approaching.explanation: Zero is 0 units from itself, so there is no other side to move to. Zero is its own opposite.
choiceFeedback: There is no separate point for -0 on the number line. Writing a negative sign in front of 0 still names the same single point, 0.
The opposite of a number is one specific number, not a whole group of them. Every number has exactly one opposite.
Zero does have an opposite. Since its distance from 0 is 0, it lands right back on itself.
hints: The opposite of a number is the same distance from 0 on the other side.
Ask yourself: how many units away from 0 is 0 itself?
If a number is 0 units from 0, moving to the other side takes you to the very same point.
approaching.explanationEs: El cero está a 0 unidades de sí mismo, así que no hay otro lado al que moverse. El cero es su propio opuesto.
choicesEs: Un número escrito -0, que es menor que 0
hintsEs: El opuesto de un número está a la misma distancia del 0, del otro lado.
Pregúntate: ¿a cuántas unidades del 0 está el 0 mismo?
Si un número está a 0 unidades del 0, moverte al otro lado te lleva al mismísimo punto.

approaching.title: Spot the Mistake: The Opposite of -7
approaching.titleEs: Encuentra el error: El opuesto de -7

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: The number starts out negative, and taking the opposite of a negative number keeps it negative, so the answer stays on the left side of 0.
workedExample.workEs: El número empieza negativo, y tomar el opuesto de un número negativo lo mantiene negativo, así que la respuesta se queda del lado izquierdo del 0.

approaching.correctWork: Opposites are the same distance from 0 but on OPPOSITE sides of 0. -7 sits 7 units to the left of 0, so its opposite must sit 7 units to the RIGHT of 0. That number is 7. The only integer that is its own opposite is 0, because 0 is zero units from itself.
approaching.correctWorkEs: Los opuestos están a la misma distancia de 0 pero en lados OPUESTOS del 0. -7 queda 7 unidades a la izquierda del 0, así que su opuesto debe quedar 7 unidades a la DERECHA del 0. Ese número es 7. El único entero que es su propio opuesto es 0, porque 0 está a cero unidades de sí mismo.
hints: What does the word 'opposite' require about which side of 0 a number is on?
Count how many units -7 is from 0, then count that same distance in the other direction.
Mark -7 on a number line, count the 7 units back to 0, then keep counting 7 more units in the same direction past 0.
approaching.explanation: The "Student thinking" step invents a rule that opposites keep their sign. The definition says the two numbers sit on opposite sides of 0, so taking an opposite always changes the direction: from the left side to the right side. The distance never changes, which is why -7 and 7 are both 7 units from 0.
approaching.explanationEs: El paso "Student thinking" inventa una regla de que los opuestos conservan su signo. La definición dice que los dos números están en lados opuestos del 0, así que tomar el opuesto siempre cambia la dirección: del lado izquierdo al lado derecho. La distancia nunca cambia, por eso -7 y 7 están ambos a 7 unidades del 0.
hintsEs: ¿Qué exige la palabra 'opuesto' sobre de qué lado del 0 está un número?
Cuenta cuántas unidades está -7 del 0, luego cuenta esa misma distancia en la otra dirección.
Marca -7 en una recta numérica, cuenta las 7 unidades de regreso al 0, y sigue contando 7 unidades más en la misma dirección pasando el 0.

approaching.stem: Which list of integers is ordered from LEAST to GREATEST?
approaching.explanation: Least to greatest reads left to right on the number line: -8, then -3, then 0, then 5.
choiceFeedback: The two negatives are swapped. Among negative integers, the one with the larger digit is farther LEFT of 0, which makes it the smaller value.
Zero is not the least value here. Every negative integer sits to the left of 0, so both negatives must come before it.
This list runs greatest to least. The question asks for the smallest value first.
hints: Least to greatest means left to right on a number line.
Split the list into negatives and positives first — every negative integer is less than 0 and less than every positive integer.
Between -8 and -3, which one is farther to the left of 0? That number starts the list.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué lista de enteros está ordenada de MENOR a MAYOR?
approaching.explanationEs: De menor a mayor se lee de izquierda a derecha en la recta numérica: -8, luego -3, luego 0 y luego 5.
hintsEs: De menor a mayor significa de izquierda a derecha en una recta numérica.
Separa primero la lista en negativos y positivos — todo entero negativo es menor que 0 y menor que cualquier entero positivo.
Entre -8 y -3, ¿cuál está más a la izquierda del 0? Ese número empieza la lista.

approaching.stem: Badwater Basin is at -86 meters. Which elevation is FARTHER below sea level than Badwater Basin?
approaching.explanation: Farther below sea level means farther to the left of 0. -120 is 120 units below 0, which is deeper than 86 units below 0.
choiceFeedback: This spot is only 40 meters below sea level, so it is closer to the surface than -86, not deeper.
Zero is sea level, the surface itself. Nothing at 0 is below sea level at all.
This elevation is 86 meters ABOVE sea level, on the opposite side of 0 from Badwater Basin.
hints: 'Farther below sea level' means farther to the left of 0 on the number line.
First rule out anything that is not negative — those are at or above sea level.
Among the negatives, compare how many units below 0 each one is. Which one goes deeper than 86?
approaching.stemEs: Badwater Basin está a -86 metros. ¿Qué elevación está MÁS abajo del nivel del mar que Badwater Basin?
approaching.explanationEs: Más abajo del nivel del mar significa más a la izquierda del 0. -120 está 120 unidades bajo 0, más profundo que 86 unidades bajo 0.
hintsEs: 'Más abajo del nivel del mar' significa más a la izquierda del 0 en la recta numérica.
Primero descarta todo lo que no sea negativo — eso está al nivel del mar o por encima.
Entre los negativos, compara cuántas unidades debajo del 0 está cada uno. ¿Cuál baja más que 86?

onLevel.title: Spot the Mistake: Reykjavik's Temperature Swing
onLevel.titleEs: Encuentra el error: El cambio de temperatura en Reikiavik

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: At 6 a.m. in Reykjavik the temperature was -12°C. At 2 p.m. it was the opposite of the 6 a.m. temperature. What was the temperature at 2 p.m.?
workedExample.workEs: A las 6 a.m. en Reikiavik la temperatura era -12°C. A las 2 p.m. era la opuesta a la de las 6 a.m. ¿Cuál era la temperatura a las 2 p.m.?

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: The opposite of a temperature should still be a cold temperature, so I keep the negative sign and just make the number bigger. That gives a temperature farther from 0.
workedExample.workEs: El opuesto de una temperatura debería seguir siendo una temperatura fría, así que conservo el signo negativo y solo hago el número más grande. Eso da una temperatura más lejos del 0.

workedExample.label: Student answer
workedExample.workEs: La temperatura a las 2 p.m. era -24°C.

onLevel.correctWork: An opposite never changes the distance from 0 — it changes only the side. -12 is 12 units to the left of 0, so its opposite is 12 units to the RIGHT of 0, which is 12°C. The 2 p.m. temperature was 12°C. (If you then take the opposite again for 11 p.m., you come back to -12°C.)
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Un opuesto nunca cambia la distancia al 0: solo cambia el lado. -12 está 12 unidades a la izquierda del 0, así que su opuesto está 12 unidades a la DERECHA del 0, o sea 12°C. La temperatura a las 2 p.m. era 12°C. (Si luego tomas el opuesto otra vez para las 11 p.m., regresas a -12°C.)
hints: Does taking an opposite change how far a number is from 0, or only which side it is on?
Count the units: -12 is 12 units from 0. Where is the point that is also 12 units from 0?
Mark -12 and count the 12 units up to 0. Continue that same 12 units above 0 and read the temperature you land on.
onLevel.explanation: The "Student thinking" step changes the distance from 0 instead of the side, so it produces a number twice as far from zero rather than its mirror image. The definition of opposite fixes the distance at 12 units and moves the point across 0, giving 12°C.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso "Student thinking" cambia la distancia al 0 en lugar del lado, así que produce un número al doble de distancia del cero en vez de su reflejo. La definición de opuesto fija la distancia en 12 unidades y mueve el punto al otro lado del 0, dando 12°C.
hintsEs: ¿Tomar el opuesto cambia qué tan lejos está un número del 0, o solo de qué lado está?
Cuenta las unidades: -12 está a 12 unidades del 0. ¿Dónde está el punto que también está a 12 unidades del 0?
Marca -12 y cuenta las 12 unidades hasta 0. Sigue esas mismas 12 unidades por encima de 0 y lee la temperatura a la que llegas.

choices: 0 is an integer, and it is its own opposite
0 is a negative integer because it is not positive
0 is a positive integer because it has no negative sign
0 is not an integer at all
onLevel.explanation: Integers are the counting numbers, their opposites, and 0. Zero is 0 units from itself, so it is its own opposite.
choiceFeedback: Negative integers are less than 0, and 0 is not less than itself. Zero is neither negative nor positive.
Positive integers are greater than 0, and 0 is not greater than itself. The missing sign does not make it positive.
Zero is explicitly part of the definition: integers are the counting numbers, their opposites, and 0.
hints: Reread the definition of integer — check whether 0 is named in it.
Positive means greater than 0 and negative means less than 0. Is 0 either one?
For the opposite, ask how many units 0 is from itself, then move that distance to the other side.
onLevel.explanationEs: Los enteros son los números para contar, sus opuestos y el 0. El cero está a 0 unidades de sí mismo, así que es su propio opuesto.
choicesEs: 0 es un entero, y es su propio opuesto
0 es un entero negativo porque no es positivo
0 es un entero positivo porque no tiene signo negativo
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la definición de entero — revisa si el 0 aparece en ella.
Positivo significa mayor que 0 y negativo significa menor que 0. ¿El 0 es alguno de los dos?
Para el opuesto, pregunta a cuántas unidades está el 0 de sí mismo, y luego muévete esa distancia al otro lado.

onLevel.stem: At 6 a.m. in Reykjavik the temperature was -12°C. At 2 p.m. it was the opposite of the 6 a.m. temperature, and at 11 p.m. it was the opposite of the 2 p.m. temperature. What were the temperatures at 2 p.m. and 11 p.m.?
onLevel.explanation: The opposite of -12 is 12, so 2 p.m. was 12°C. The opposite of 12 is -12, so 11 p.m. was back to -12°C.
choiceFeedback: The two times are switched. The first opposite is taken from -12, so 2 p.m. has to land on the positive side of 0.
The 2 p.m. reading is right, but the second step doubled the distance from 0 instead of crossing back over 0. The opposite of 12 keeps the distance 12.
Zero is its own opposite, so the opposite of -12 cannot be 0. An opposite stays the same distance from 0, which is 12 units here.
hints: Take the opposites one step at a time — start with the 6 a.m. reading.
An opposite keeps the same distance from 0 and changes only the side, so -12 becomes a positive number that is still 12 units from 0.
Now take the opposite of your 2 p.m. answer. What happens when you take the opposite of an opposite?
onLevel.stemEs: A las 6 a.m. en Reikiavik la temperatura era -12°C. A las 2 p.m. era la opuesta a la de las 6 a.m., y a las 11 p.m. era la opuesta a la de las 2 p.m. ¿Cuáles eran las temperaturas a las 2 p.m. y a las 11 p.m.?
onLevel.explanationEs: El opuesto de -12 es 12, así que a las 2 p.m. era 12°C. El opuesto de 12 es -12, así que a las 11 p.m. volvió a -12°C.
hintsEs: Toma los opuestos paso a paso — empieza con la lectura de las 6 a. m.
Un opuesto conserva la misma distancia del 0 y solo cambia de lado, así que -12 se convierte en un número positivo que sigue a 12 unidades del 0.
Ahora toma el opuesto de tu respuesta de las 2 p. m. ¿Qué pasa cuando tomas el opuesto de un opuesto?

onLevel.stem: A football team starts at the line of scrimmage, which is 0. During one series they had a 10-yard loss, a 4-yard gain, a 3-yard loss, and a 21-yard gain. Where does the series leave them?
choices: 12 yards past the line of scrimmage
8 yards past the line of scrimmage
18 yards past the line of scrimmage
38 yards past the line of scrimmage
onLevel.explanation: Write each play as an integer: -10, 4, -3, 21. Combining them gives -10 + 4 - 3 + 21 = 12, so the team ends 12 yards past the line of scrimmage.
choiceFeedback: The 4-yard gain got left out of the count. Every play changes the team's position, gains and losses alike.
The 3-yard loss was counted as a gain here. A loss moves the team backward, so it is a negative integer.
This adds all four plays as if every one were a gain. Losses have to be written as negative integers before you combine them.
hints: The line of scrimmage is 0. Which plays move the team below 0, and which move it above?
Write all four plays as integers first: gains are positive and losses are negative.
Combine -10, 4, -3, and 21 in order, keeping every sign. Where do you land compared to 0?
onLevel.stemEs: Un equipo de fútbol americano empieza en la línea de golpeo, que es 0. En una serie tuvo una pérdida de 10 yardas, una ganancia de 4 yardas, una pérdida de 3 yardas y una ganancia de 21 yardas. ¿Dónde termina la serie?
onLevel.explanationEs: Escribe cada jugada como entero: -10, 4, -3, 21. Al combinarlos: -10 + 4 - 3 + 21 = 12, así que el equipo termina 12 yardas más allá de la línea de golpeo.
choicesEs: 12 yardas más allá de la línea de golpeo
8 yardas más allá de la línea de golpeo
18 yardas más allá de la línea de golpeo
38 yardas más allá de la línea de golpeo
hintsEs: La línea de golpeo es 0. ¿Cuáles jugadas mueven al equipo debajo de 0 y cuáles por encima?
Escribe primero las cuatro jugadas como enteros: las ganancias son positivas y las pérdidas negativas.
Combina -10, 4, -3 y 21 en orden, conservando cada signo. ¿Dónde caes en comparación con 0?

onLevel.prompt: Describe two different real-world situations that use negative integers. For each one, tell exactly what 0 means in that situation, write one negative integer it could produce, and explain what the opposite of that integer would mean in the same situation.
onLevel.promptEs: Describe dos situaciones del mundo real distintas que usen enteros negativos. Para cada una, di exactamente qué significa 0 en esa situación, escribe un entero negativo que podría producir y explica qué significaría el opuesto de ese entero en la misma situación.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: My first situation is ___. In it, 0 means ___, so ___ would represent ___. The opposite of that integer is ___, which would mean ___.
onLevel.hint: Pick situations where something can be measured both above and below a natural starting point.
hints: Think about places where a measurement can go both above and below a starting point: elevation, temperature, money, football yardage.
Name the starting point out loud — that is your 0. Then a quantity below it is your negative integer.
For the opposite, keep the same distance from 0 and cross to the other side, then say what that new number means in your story.
onLevel.explanation: Every situation that uses negative integers has a chosen zero. With elevation, 0 is sea level, so -30 meters means 30 meters below the surface and its opposite, 30, means 30 meters above it. With temperature, 0 is zero degrees, so -5°C is five degrees below zero and its opposite, 5°C, is five degrees above. In both cases the opposite is the same distance from 0, just measured in the other direction, which is what makes it the mirror image of the original quantity.
onLevel.explanationEs: Toda situación que usa enteros negativos tiene un cero elegido. Con la elevación, 0 es el nivel del mar, así que -30 metros significa 30 metros bajo la superficie y su opuesto, 30, significa 30 metros por encima. Con la temperatura, 0 es cero grados, así que -5°C son cinco grados bajo cero y su opuesto, 5°C, son cinco grados arriba. En ambos casos el opuesto está a la misma distancia del 0, solo medido en la otra dirección, y eso lo convierte en el reflejo de la cantidad original.
hintsEs: Piensa en lugares donde una medida puede ir por encima y por debajo de un punto de partida: elevación, temperatura, dinero, yardas de fútbol americano.
Di en voz alta cuál es el punto de partida — ese es tu 0. Luego una cantidad por debajo de él es tu entero negativo.
Para el opuesto, conserva la misma distancia del 0 y cruza al otro lado, luego di qué significa ese número nuevo en tu historia.

onLevel.instructionsEs: Escribe el entero que representa cada situación. Recuerda decidir primero qué significa 0.
rows: A football play with a 12-yard loss
A hiker 250 meters above sea level
A submarine resting at the surface of the water
onLevel.hint: Decide what 0 means in the situation, then check whether the quantity is above it or below it.
hints: Each row describes a quantity measured from a starting point. That starting point is 0.
Words like 'loss' and 'below' put the quantity under 0; words like 'above' put it over 0.
Row 1 measures from the line of scrimmage, and a loss moves backward from it — so the integer needs a negative sign.
onLevel.explanation: Each situation has a natural 0: the line of scrimmage, sea level, zero degrees, and the water surface. A 12-yard loss moves backward from the line of scrimmage, so it is -12. A hiker 250 meters above sea level is +250, written simply as 250. Seven degrees below zero is -7. A submarine resting right at the surface is exactly at the starting point, so its integer is 0 — not positive and not negative.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada situación tiene un 0 natural: la línea de golpeo, el nivel del mar, cero grados y la superficie del agua. Una pérdida de 12 yardas retrocede desde la línea de golpeo, así que es -12. Un excursionista a 250 metros sobre el nivel del mar es +250, que se escribe simplemente 250. Siete grados bajo cero es -7. Un submarino justo en la superficie está exactamente en el punto de partida, así que su entero es 0: ni positivo ni negativo.
hintsEs: Cada fila describe una cantidad medida desde un punto de partida. Ese punto de partida es 0.
Palabras como 'pérdida' y 'debajo' ponen la cantidad bajo 0; palabras como 'arriba' la ponen sobre 0.
La fila 1 mide desde la línea de golpeo, y una pérdida se mueve hacia atrás desde ahí — así que el entero necesita signo negativo.

practice.commonMistake: The most common mistake in this lesson is thinking that the opposite of a negative integer is still negative — for example, saying the opposite of -7 is -7, or that the opposite of -12 is -24. Opposites are the same DISTANCE from 0 but on OPPOSITE sides of 0, so taking an opposite always changes the direction and never changes the distance: the opposite of -7 is 7 and the opposite of -12 is 12. The one exception is 0, which is 0 units from itself and is therefore its own opposite. Before you submit, count the units from 0 and check that your answer is on the other side.

connect.scenario: To make a first down, a football team must gain at least 10 yards from where they started, a spot called the line of scrimmage. The line of scrimmage is 0: a gain moves the team above 0 and a loss moves the team below 0. During one series, a team had a 10-yard loss, a 4-yard gain, a 3-yard loss, and a 21-yard gain.
connect.promptQuestion: Write each play as an integer, then decide: did the team make a first down, and how far are they from the line of scrimmage?
connect.prompt: The 10-yard loss is the integer ___ and the 3-yard loss is the integer ___. Combining all four plays leaves the team ___ yards from where they started, which is ___ the line of scrimmage. Because they needed at least 10 yards, the team ___ make a first down.

check.stem: Which integer represents a 3-yard loss when the line of scrimmage is 0?
check.explanation: A loss moves the team backward from the line of scrimmage, which is below 0, so it is written with a negative sign: -3.

check.stem: The four plays are -10, 4, -3, and 21. What is the team's net result?
check.explanation: -10 + 4 - 3 + 21 = 12, so the team ended up 12 yards past the line of scrimmage.

check.stem: What does 0 represent in this football situation?
choices: The line of scrimmage, the spot where the series started
A play in which nobody touched the ball
The end zone at the edge of the field
The number of yards still needed for a first down
check.explanation: Every play is measured from the spot the team started, so that spot is 0. Gains are positive integers above it and losses are negative integers below it.

connect.modelAnswer: The four plays as integers are -10, 4, -3, and 21, because a loss is below the line of scrimmage (0) and a gain is above it. Combining them: -10 + 4 - 3 + 21 = 12. The team ends 12 yards past the line of scrimmage. Since a first down needs at least 10 yards and 12 is greater than 10, the team DID make a first down. Writing the losses as negative integers is what makes this work — if you counted all four plays as gains you would get 38, which would say the team traveled nearly four first downs.

diagram.title: Each Play Measured From the Line of Scrimmage
diagram.caption: 0 is the line of scrimmage. Losses are negative integers to the left of 0, gains are positive integers to the right, and 12 marks where the series ended.

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: Which situation is best represented by the integer -15?
choices: A diver 15 meters below the surface of the water
A hill 15 meters above sea level
A deposit of $15 into a bank account
A football play with a 15-yard gain
exitTicket.explanation: A negative integer represents a quantity below the chosen 0. With the water surface as 0, a diver 15 meters below it is -15.
choiceFeedback: Above sea level is above 0, so this is +15, not -15.
A deposit adds money to the account, which moves the balance above 0. A withdrawal would be the negative one.
A gain moves the team forward from the line of scrimmage, so it is +15. A loss would be negative.
hints: A negative integer describes a quantity BELOW whatever 0 stands for.
For each choice, name the 0 first: sea level, the water surface, an empty account, the line of scrimmage.
Look for the one situation whose words point downward or backward from that starting point.

warmup.spiralFrom: Number lines and distance from zero

questions.stem: On a number line, which number is farther from 0: 3 or 7?
choices: You cannot tell from a number line
questions.explanation: Distance from 0 is how many units you count. 7 is 7 units from 0; 3 is only 3 units.

questions.stem: Start at 0 on a number line and count 6 units to the right. Where do you land?
questions.explanation: Each unit is one step, so 6 steps to the right of 0 lands on 6.

questions.stem: Two points on a number line are each 4 units from 0 — one to the left and one to the right. How far apart are the two points?
questions.explanation: Each point is 4 units from 0, so going from one to the other passes 4 units to reach 0 and 4 more after it: 4 + 4 = 8.

questions.stem: A thermometer marks 0 degrees. Which phrase describes a temperature WARMER than 0 degrees?
questions.explanation: Warmer means higher on the scale, which is above the 0 mark. "Far from 0" could be either direction.
